headline: PHP2Shell Exploitation Leads a Day of Session and Supply-Chain Risk
standfirst: Exploitation of two critical PHP flaws leads the briefing, with industrial vendors confirming exposure to the same issue. A Brotli decoder flaw forces cross-ecosystem patching, while token theft and exposed keys dominate the breach reporting.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

Two critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and tracked as PHP2Shell, have been successfully exploited in the wild, according to [[s26]]. Both NVD entries carry a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 Critical, with network attack vector, high attack complexity, no required privileges and no user interaction. NVD lists vulnerable PHP ranges ending before 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. The story does not supply exploit mechanics, targeted victims or the initial access path. The supplied KEV fields do not list either CVE, so the in-the-wild claim rests on the story text, not CISA catalog membership.

CERT-UA says attackers compromised internet-connected Dahua cameras and video recorders, changed their settings and created unauthorized user accounts, [[s11]]. No CVE, exploit chain or post-compromise objective is supplied. Analysis: exposed surveillance gear is useful as a foothold because it is often internet-facing and poorly monitored, but the excerpt does not establish what these particular attackers did beyond account creation.

## Vulnerabilities

An out-of-bounds write in Google's Brotli decoder affects Node.js, .NET, PowerShell and Python packages and can lead to code execution, driving patching across those ecosystems, [[s23]]. The supplied structured intelligence gives no CVE ID, CVSS score or affected versions, so this briefing cannot rank its severity or confirm exploitation. The story uses the name Node2Shell, but the excerpt does not add exploitation status or patch detail. Analysis: the notable factor is breadth — one decoder defect reaches multiple language runtimes and package sets — while the excerpt does not describe an attack campaign.

Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB and others have confirmed that some of their products are affected by PHP2Shell, [[s8]]. That carries the same PHP2Shell flaws into industrial product lines, but the excerpt does not identify specific products, versions or remediation. Treat the industrial exposure as confirmed at the vendor level only, not as evidence of exploitation in those products.

## Breaches

An adversary-in-the-middle relay captured Microsoft 365 sign-in sessions and replayed stolen tokens to break into email accounts at 79 organizations, compromising 97 accounts, [[s28]]. The activity included 497 successful Microsoft 365 sign-in events, according to the story. The excerpt does not give victim sectors, the relay's delivery method or the MFA configuration of affected tenants, so the excerpt does not establish an MFA bypass. Analysis: replaying a post-authentication session is potent because it reuses trust already granted, but the supplied evidence stops short of explaining how the relay was positioned.

LiteLLM says an accidentally exposed key that was not revoked was behind a supply-chain attack believed to have hit tens of thousands of users, [[s18]]. The story describes an open-source AI tool with a large downstream user base; it does not supply a confirmed victim count, the malicious payload or remediation. The word "believed" matters: the scale is an estimate, not a confirmed tally.

An automated campaign called Gheist is using stolen GitHub tokens to plant workflows that print repository secrets into GitHub Actions logs, which attackers then download before deleting the runs, [[s29]]. The activity succeeded in private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments, according to the analysis. The excerpt cuts off a description of a GitHub safeguard, so its effect is not established here. No CVE or actor attribution beyond the campaign name is supplied.

Quest Diagnostics confirmed that patient records were exposed after unauthorized access to its Quanum LSM system, [[s34]]. The excerpt does not give the number of records, affected population, intrusion method or remediation. That leaves the healthcare impact material but not quantifiable from this evidence.

nvd.description: PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

selected.angle: The PHP2Shell RCE flaws have moved from disclosure to real attacks, raising urgency for any internet-facing PHP deployment.

The flaw can let an attacker corrupt memory and potentially run code. nvd.description:
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.





Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.
